Gina / Aditya — thanks, I reviewed the Novum redlines. High-level position and proposed language below.

Position: Redwood is willing to accept a limited, narrowly-tailored carve-out to the liability cap for confidentiality breaches that involve (1) proven unauthorized access or disclosure of Customer trade secrets or PHI and (2) direct, documented losses reasonably attributable to that breach. We are not comfortable with an uncapped exposure for broad "consequential" categories; instead we propose a two-tier approach:

- Tier A (Trade secret/PHI theft): carve-out from the cap for direct damages arising from intentional or grossly negligent unauthorized acquisition or disclosure of the customer's trade secrets or PHI, subject to a high-burden-of-proof standard (investigation, external counsel confirmation, forensic report).
- Tier B (Related consequential losses): allow recovery of consequential damages only where Novum provides written, contemporaneous evidence tying the consequential loss to the breach (e.g., regulatory fines or third-party claims directly resulting from the disclosed trade secret/PHI). Recoverable consequential damages should be limited to (i) third-party claims the customer is obligated to pay and (ii) documented remediation costs.

Proposed contract snippet (suggested redline for Section 10.3):
"Notwithstanding any other provision, liability arising from an unauthorized disclosure or access to Customer's trade secrets or PHI shall be excluded from the limitations on liability set forth in this Agreement to the extent such liability arises from direct damages established by a qualified forensic investigation and confirmation by independent counsel. Consequential damages shall be recoverable only where the Customer provides documented evidence that such damages were proximately caused by the confirmed disclosure and are limited to third-party liabilities and documented remediation costs."

Evidence: we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (attached in shared drive link) and a 2-page controls summary. We cannot provide incident histories beyond a confidential summary, but we can state whether we have had material confidentiality incidents in the last 36 months (we have none to disclose).

Process: if Novum accepts the two-tier approach, we will prepare the redline and a short evidence packet (SOC2 link + controls summary + signed statement re: incidents) and route for signature. If Novum insists on uncapped consequential damages, we'll need a procurement-approved risk exception and insurance confirmation.

Laura — please add any notes on remedial caps or insurance language.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Neha / Aditya / Gina — thanks for the thoughtful proposal. Novum's Counsel has reviewed the two-tier approach and is generally receptive to the forensic + counsel confirmation requirement for Tier A, provided the contract clarifies timelines for forensic validation and dispute resolution steps. They also propose adding a narrowly tailored carve-out for regulatory fines where a proven disclosure triggers regulator action — subject to Redwood's right to defend and mitigate.

I've attached a single markup that merges Novum's requested redlines and Neha's language. Key outstanding items:
- Forensic timeline: Novum requests initial forensic report within 30 days of discovery; Redwood prefers 45 days.
- Insurance/indemnity overlap: Novum is asking that third-party regulatory fines be recoverable; Redwood's team requests that recoverable regulatory penalties be limited to those that are insurable under Redwood's primary policy and subject to mitigation.
- DocuSign: Novum procurement will finalize the Order Form once MSA redlines settle — they will send a DocuSign link.

If you want to short-call to resolve the forensic timeline, I can make time Monday morning.
